These materials are designed for **self-paced, optional practice**. You can use a single section, follow several exercises in sequence, or consult a reference only when you need it. Nothing here requires completing a formal assessment.

## Getting started with R

- [Hands-On Programming with R — Getting Started](https://rstudio-education.github.io/hopr/starting.html): installation, RStudio and first commands.
- [R for Data Science (2e)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/), by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund: extensive explanations and worked exercises. Especially useful are [workflow basics](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-basics.html), [data transformation](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html), [data tidying](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-tidy.html), [visualization layers](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/layers.html), [exploratory data analysis](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/EDA.html), and [code style](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-style.html).
- [R project](https://www.r-project.org/), [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/): official software and package information.
- [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/): creating `.qmd` documents, rendering R code, and [publishing on GitHub Pages](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html). Quarto is used to publish these materials; learners do not need it merely to run R exercises.

## Packages used in these exercises

- [`refugees` package](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/), including its documentation for [population](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/reference/population.html), [applications](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/reference/asylum_applications.html) and [decisions](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/reference/asylum_decisions.html).
- [`dplyr`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/) for transforming and aggregating data; [`tidyr`](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/) for reshaping and joins-related workflows.
- [`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) for graphics; [`scales`](https://scales.r-lib.org/) for displaying numeric quantities and percentages.
- [`broom`](https://broom.tidymodels.org/) for extracting model results into tables; [`stargazer` on CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=stargazer) and [`modelsummary`](https://modelsummary.com/) for regression tables; [`sandwich`](https://sandwich.r-forge.r-project.org/) and [`lmtest`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=lmtest) for selected model diagnostics and standard-error calculations.

Package names on this page are **tools**, not recommendations that everyone must learn or install every package. The inference exercises identify the additional packages they need.

## Refugee statistics and definitions

- [UNHCR Refugee Data Finder](https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/): official portal to explore reported refugee and asylum statistics and methodological information.
- [UNHCR Data Visualization Guidance](https://dataviz.unhcr.org/): practical advice on displaying displacement statistics clearly.
- Always check the **underlying definition** before reusing a number: end-of-year stock versus annual applications or decisions; origin versus asylum country; reported persons versus cases; initial versus appeal level; and treatment of non-substantive decisions.

## Attribution and limitations

The fixed ten-origin 2022 example in `data/unhcr_origin_top10_2022.csv` reproduces values used in the `refugees` package documentation for the combined `refugees + oip` measure. These are **selected origin observations**, not a random sample of all origins. The dataset `data/toy_asylum_decisions.csv`, together with fictional jurisdiction and claim-level examples, exists **only for learning** and must not be treated as real asylum evidence.

Other calculations are generated when the teaching materials are rendered against the installed `refugees` package version. Results may change when the package or its source data are updated. The materials are independently prepared; they are **not an official UNHCR statistical product or an institutional statement on behalf of UCD**.

These explanations and exercises are original teaching material, informed by the pedagogical approach of *R for Data Science*; they do not reproduce its text or illustrations. When drawing on R packages or published datasets in research, cite their documentation and primary sources as appropriate.

## Recording a reproducible analysis

For an exercise or research output, keep the R script (or `.qmd` source), the data source, the date and definitions used, and relevant software versions. For example:

```{r}
#| eval: false
packageVersion("refugees")
R.version.string
sessionInfo()
```

`sessionInfo()` also records the session's loaded packages and platform information. For work intended to be rerun long after publication, also consider saving a package-version lockfile (for example using `renv`) and recording source-data release/version information when available. A saved script does not by itself resolve missingness, sampling, or cross-country comparability concerns.
